name: Geierwally Freilichtbühne Elbigenalp
kurzbeschreibung: The Geierwally Open-Air Stage in Elbigenalp: spectacular outdoor theatre in the wild Bernhardstal gorge, honoring Anna Stainer-Knittel.
beschreibung:
Overview

The dramatic Geierwally Open-Air Stage is deeply embedded in the rugged rock faces of the romantic Bernhardstal gorge in Elbigenalp in Tyrol's Lechtal valley, at an altitude of around 1,040 meters above sea level. Founded in 1993, this regionally celebrated natural stage is one of the most extraordinary and atmospheric cultural venues in the entire Alpine region. Built in honor of the famous Lechtal painter and pioneer Anna Stainer-Knittel (1841–1915) – who became world-famous as the legendary “Geierwally” through Wilhelmine von Hillern's novel – the stage annually captivates thousands of theatre and culture enthusiasts from all over Central Europe. The unique setting and gripping productions make every visit an unforgettable experience.

Route & Requirements

The historical inspiration for the stage is based on a true event: as a 17-year-old girl in 1858, Anna Stainer-Knittel descended a vertical rock face in the Lechtal Alps, secured by a rope, to raid an eagle's nest – a daring feat that no man dared to attempt at the time. From this event, literature created the archetype of the courageous, unyielding Alpine heroine. The open-air stage uses the vertical limestone cliffs of the Bernhardstal gorge and the rushing of the Bernhardstalbach stream as a monumental, natural backdrop.

Visit & Arrival

The theatre season at the Geierwally Open-Air Stage runs annually from early July to late August with performances on weekends (Friday to Sunday, usually starting at 20:30; afternoon performances on Sundays at 15:00). Ticket prices for theatre performances (as of season 2025/2026): approx. €28.00 to €38.00 depending on the category. Outside of performance times, the gorge area and the themed trail are freely and cost-free accessible during the day. Arrival by car: Via the B198 (Lechtalstraße) from Reutte or Warth to Elbigenalp; large free parking spaces are available in the village center at the community center (from there, about a 10-minute leisurely walk into the Bernhardstal gorge).

Tips

The illuminated path through the gorge to the grandstand is wide and gravelled, and with some assistance, it is also accessible for wheelchair users (special wheelchair spaces are available in the covered theatre area). Since the performances take place in a cool mountain gorge, it is advisable to bring a warm jacket or blanket even on warm summer days. Book theatre tickets well in advance, as many performances are sold out weeks beforehand. Allow sufficient time for arrival and the short walk to fully enjoy the unique atmosphere before the performance.
